Telescope 3.0 is the biggest update so far. Your phone can now be your computer's microphone too, Telescope can stream only while a call actually needs the camera, and from here on both apps update themselves.

## Before you upgrade from 2.3

This one takes a couple of minutes by hand. After that, updates are one click.

- **Uninstall the old phone app first.** 3.0 is signed differently, so Android won't install it over 2.3. Uninstall Telescope on the phone, then install the new `Telescope.apk`.
- **Pair your phone again.** Pairing works differently now (see below), so old pairings don't carry over. Neither do the settings 2.3 kept per phone: camera, resolution and FPS, flip and zoom, and the battery and temperature alerts. The virtual camera size in Advanced carries over.
- **Windows:** Telescope now comes as a folder instead of a single exe. Extract the whole zip somewhere permanent and run `TelescopeDesktop.exe` from inside it. You can delete the old exe.
- **Windows:** the webcam is now called **Telescope** in other apps. If it still shows the old name, open **Advanced** and click **Rename**.

## New

**Your phone as a microphone.** Turn on Microphone and the phone's mic shows up on your computer as "Telescope Microphone". On Windows this needs the free VB-Cable driver, and Telescope links you to it.

**Automatic streaming.** Telescope can start the stream by itself when Discord, OBS, Zoom or anything else opens the camera, or as soon as your phone is ready, and stop it once nothing has used the camera for a while. Your phone doesn't have to run the camera all day. You pick when it starts, when it stops and how long it waits, under **Automatic streaming** in the settings menu. Telescope can also open by itself when you sign in.

**Wait for my computer.** Turn this on in the phone app and your computer can start the stream even while the phone is locked or the app is closed. It's off by default, and a notification shows while it's waiting.

**Wait screen.** Apps now see a proper picture while nothing is streaming, instead of a frozen frame or black. Use the default one or pick your own image or GIF, and mirror it if it comes out backwards.

**Updates.** The desktop and phone apps check for updates at launch and install them for you. If an update gets cut short or the new version won't start, Telescope goes back to the one that worked. With the phone plugged in, the desktop can update the phone app over USB.

**Presets.** Save your camera, zoom and output settings as a preset and switch between them in one click, even mid-stream. Each phone keeps its own.

**Better zoom.** Zoom now happens on the phone's sensor, not by cropping on the computer, so the picture stays sharper. On phones with several lenses, **Auto** switches to the telephoto when your framing fits in it. Dots on the zoom slider show where each lens takes over, and a small dot next to the zoom value shows which lens you're on.

**Pan and zoom in the preview.** Scroll over the preview to zoom, drag to pan, and click anywhere to focus there.

**H.264.** An optional stream format that uses much less bandwidth than MJPEG. Worth trying on busy Wi-Fi.

**Encrypted connection.** Everything between the phone and the computer is now encrypted, and locked to the computer you paired with.

## Easier to set up and use

- A setup checklist walks you through the virtual camera, the phone app and pairing on first launch.
- Pair over Wi-Fi by scanning a QR code, or just plug the phone in over USB. One phone can pair with several computers.
- Telescope picks USB or Wi-Fi by itself and tells you which one it's using. If a cable is plugged in but not being used, it tells you why.
- If the stream drops, Telescope keeps looking for the phone over every route, so pulling the cable carries on over Wi-Fi.
- When something stops a stream from starting, a banner in the window says what's wrong and gives you a button to fix it.
- The phone app asks for permissions in one setup card instead of a pile of prompts at launch, and it's trimmed down to what the computer doesn't already control.
- Telescope can stop the stream when the phone's battery runs low or it gets too hot. Each alert has its own switch for the notification and for stopping.
- On Linux, the virtual camera asks for your password once, not every time. Telescope also shows up in the app menu.
- **Copy diagnostics** on both apps gives you a report to paste into a bug report, without your addresses or pairing codes.

## Fixed

- Much lower delay, and 4K MJPEG now keeps up.
- The phone showing as unreachable even though it worked over USB (#13).
- Terminal windows popping up over and over on Windows (#26).
- Screen flashing in some apps when they opened the camera on Windows.
- The Windows app starting slowly.
- One bad value in the settings file stopping Telescope from starting at all.
- The phone app getting stuck in a half-stopped stream after another app took the camera.
- Switching lens in manual exposure quietly changing ISO and shutter speed.
- On Linux, `start.sh` only goes online when dependencies change, and a failed install no longer stops Telescope from opening.
- Both apps now recover by themselves from stuck states, like a phone stuck starting or a camera failing mid-stream, instead of needing a restart.
- Lots of smaller fixes around connecting, pairing and saving settings.

Found something broken? Open an issue and paste your **Copy diagnostics** report into it.
